represented_space.row_column_convention: matrix row is the canonical source site and matrix column is the canonical target site

route_A_centered_uniform.twist_metadata: centered lift phi_c in [-1/2,1/2); every frozen D4 image remains in this domain
route_A_centered_uniform.hamiltonian_rule: for retained hopping R and source x, target y=x+R modulo N receives h_R*exp(2*pi*i*(phi_c,x*R_x/N_x + phi_c,y*R_y/N_y))
route_A_centered_uniform.translation_rule: uniform-link matrices remain exactly translation covariant
route_A_centered_uniform.limitation: no claim is made for continuity or a fixed matrix gauge across the centered-domain boundary

route_B_reduced_seam.hamiltonian_rule: if x+R=y+N*q with canonical y, the retained hopping receives h_R*exp(2*pi*i*q dot bar_phi)
route_B_reduced_seam.prohibition: Route B must be constructed from seam crossings and must not be generated by similarity transformation of Route A

gauge_bridge.role: deterministic equivalence relation, not a third independent numerical vote
gauge_bridge.lift_rule: phi_tilde is retained before reduction; bar_phi is componentwise phi_tilde modulo one; n=phi_tilde-bar_phi is retained as an exact integer pair
gauge_bridge.uniform_representative_rule: uniform matrices at integer-equivalent lifts are related by the exact diagonal gauge derived from their retained lifts
gauge_bridge.recovered_defect_rule: after each route applies its own known inverse and reference correction, the recovered point-onsite matrices agree directly because diagonal site gauges commute with scalar onsite projectors
comparison_metrics: canonical bridge maximum-entry and Frobenius defects
attacked bridge maximum-entry and Frobenius defects
matrix SHA-256 identities after explicitly declared gauge conversion

case_inventory.ordering: route A then route B for retained route-local records; matched comparisons use the frozen 18-case order

known_map_contract.route_local_rule: each route constructs, attacks, inversely aligns, subtracts, and classifies its own matrices without using the other route
known_map_contract.cross_route_rule: compare raw canonical and attacked matrices only through the declared bridge; compare recovered scalar onsite defects directly

blind_alignment_contract.cross_route_requirement: ordered ambiguity map identities, issue codes, null selected maps, null extracted operators, and shift diagnostics agree; counts alone are insufficient

schedules: fresh spawned process: Route A, then Route B, then bridge
separate fresh spawned process: Route B, then Route A, then bridge
schedule_isolation: identical immutable input bytes and tolerances
no output, cache, matrix, inferred phase, ambiguity set, or diagnostic is shared between schedule processes
each route constructs its own matrices from the frozen compact inputs
bridge evaluation begins only after both route-local outputs exist inside that schedule
retained serialization order is canonical Route A, Route B, bridge regardless of execution schedule
required_clean_behavior: Route A records agree between schedules within algebraic_absolute
Route B records agree between schedules within algebraic_absolute
bridge records agree between schedules within route_equivalence_absolute
ordered ambiguity identities and all criterion dispositions are identical
canonical serialized schedule-independent projection is byte-identical
